newsitem.title: JAPAN: IBJ April 1.6% 5-year debenture traded at 2.27%.
newsitem.headline: IBJ April 1.6% 5-year debenture traded at 2.27%.

text.p: The Industrial Bank of Japan's (IBJ) 1.60 percent five-year debenture issued in April was traded at a yield of 2.27 percent late on Friday morning, sharply up from Thursday's 2.03 percent, traders said.
An IBJ spokesman said the bank would announce its long-term prime lending rate for May next Monday as scheduled.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
Traders said that if the yield of the April IBJ debenture stayed at the current level, the May prime rate may be raised by 0.6 or 0.7 percentage point from 2.5 percent in April.
The prime rate is usually set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon of IBJ's five-year debenture, which is issued monthly and is the benchmark in Japan's debenture market.
Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
